marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q019.takeaway: Afferent arteriolar dilation raises both renal plasma flow and glomerular capillary pressure, increasing GFR.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q019.displayText:
Afferent arteriolar dilation raises both renal plasma flow and glomerular capillary pressure, increasing GFR.

Dilation of the afferent arteriole will increase both GFR and RPF.

+ Increase renal plasma flow (RPF) - because renal vascular resistance is decreased

¢ Increase glomerular filtration rate (GFR) - because glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure is

increased.

¢ Filtration fraction (FF) remains normal

Dilation of the efferent arteriole will increase RPF but decrease GFR.
emphasis: Afferent arteriolar dilation raises both renal plasma flow and glomerular capillary pressure, increasing GFR

rationales.a: Hyperproteinemia raises plasma oncotic pressure and opposes filtration rather than reliably increasing both GFR and RPF.
rationales.b: Efferent constriction can increase GFR but typically reduces renal plasma flow.
rationales.c: Efferent dilation increases flow but lowers glomerular capillary pressure and GFR.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q025.takeaway: Filtration fraction = GFR/RPF; use inulin for GFR and PAH for effective RPF.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q025.displayText:
Filtration fraction = GFR/RPF; use inulin for GFR and PAH for effective RPF.

Inulin and PAHA are used to determine the filtration fraction. The filtration fraction is the ratio of
GFR and RPF
Inulin, a polymer of fructose can be used to measure GFR. Para-aminohippuric acid (PAHA) is
used to measure RPF.
emphasis: Filtration fraction = GFR/RPF; use inulin for GFR and PAH for effective RPF

rationales.b: Urea is reabsorbed and cannot provide a clean GFR measurement; diodrast is not the selected standard pair.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q026.takeaway: The myogenic response to stretch depolarizes afferent arteriolar smooth muscle and opens voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels, causing contraction.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q026.displayText:
The myogenic response to stretch depolarizes afferent arteriolar smooth muscle and opens voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels, causing contraction.

The afferent arterioles contract in response to stretch induced by the opening of calcium channels.
The mechanism is called myogenic autoregulation of renal blood flow and GFR.
The stretch of the vascular wall allows increased movement of calcium ions from the extracellular
fluid into the cells, causing them to contract. This contraction prevents excessive stretch of the
vessel. This prevents excessive increase of renal blood flow and GFR by raising vascular
resistance.
This mechanism may be more important in protecting the kidney from hypertension-induced
injury.
Autoregulation has two main mechanisms:
¢ Metabolic mechanism: Tissues produce vasodilatory metabolites that regulate flow eg.
prostaglandins, NO, CO2, H+ and K+ NS

rationales.b: Noradrenaline can constrict vessels but is not the intrinsic myogenic response.
rationales.d: Adenosine participates in tubuloglomerular feedback, not the primary stretch-triggered myogenic pathway.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q029.takeaway: During shock, renal sympathetic tone raises afferent arteriolar resistance to conserve circulating volume, reducing renal flow/GFR.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q029.displayText:
During shock, renal sympathetic tone raises afferent arteriolar resistance to conserve circulating volume, reducing renal flow/GFR.

Kidney responds to shock by increasing afferent arteriolar resistance.
During shock, both afferent and efferent arterioles in kidney are constricted, however, the efferent
vessels are constricted much more.
The glomerular filtration rate and the plasma renal flow is decreased during shock. As plasma
renal flow is decreased to a greater extent, the filtration fraction increases. (Option 1 & 3)
emphasis: During shock, renal sympathetic tone raises afferent arteriolar resistance to conserve circulating volume, reducing renal flow/GFR

rationales.a: The kidney does not increase renal blood flow during systemic shock; sympathetic vasoconstriction reduces it.
rationales.c: GFR is not increased during shock; perfusion falls.
rationales.d: Only increased afferent resistance is correct; the paired increase in GFR is false.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q032.takeaway: Heparan sulfate proteoglycans contribute negative charge to the glomerular basement membrane and repel anionic proteins.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q032.displayText:
Heparan sulfate proteoglycans contribute negative charge to the glomerular basement membrane and repel anionic proteins.

The protein in the glomerular basement membrane responsible for charge-dependent filtration is
heparan sulfate. It prevents filtration by repelling negatively charged proteins.
Collagen type IV, fibronectin, entactin are structural components of basement membrane.
emphasis: Heparan sulfate proteoglycans contribute negative charge to the glomerular basement membrane and repel anionic proteins

rationales.a: Fibronectin is an ECM adhesion protein, not the principal charge-selective GBM molecule named here.
rationales.c: Type IV collagen forms the GBM scaffold but the charge-selective component is heparan sulfate.
rationales.d: Entactin/nidogen links matrix components and is not the named anionic filtration determinant.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q033.takeaway: Efferent constriction raises glomerular hydrostatic pressure and filtration fraction; increased capillary oncotic pressure is expected, so its decrease is the exception.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q033.displayText:
Efferent constriction raises glomerular hydrostatic pressure and filtration fraction; increased capillary oncotic pressure is expected, so its decrease is the exception.

Efferent arteriolar constriction increases oncotic pressure in glomerular capillaries.
Efferent arteriolar constriction has a biphasic response on GFR depending on the severity of
resistance.

Moderate efferent arteriolar constriction causes increased glomerular hydrostatic pressure and
slightly increased GFR.
However, in cases of severe efferent arteriolar constriction (more than threefold increase in
efferent arteriolar resistance), the renal blood flow is significantly reduced. This results in
increased plasma protein concentration, thereby increasing the glomerular colloid oncotic
pressure. As the increase in colloid oncotic pressure exceeds the increase in hydrostatic pressure,
the net force for filtration decreases, resulting in decreased GFR.
emphasis: Efferent constriction raises glomerular hydrostatic pressure and filtration fraction; increased capillary oncotic pressure is expected, so its decrease is the exception

rationales.a: GFR usually rises with moderate efferent constriction; severe constriction can eventually reduce it.
rationales.b: Renal blood flow falls as efferent resistance increases.
rationales.d: Glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure increases with efferent constriction.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q034.takeaway: A ureteric stone raises downstream tubular/Bowman pressure and opposes filtration, so it does not increase GFR.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q034.displayText:
A ureteric stone raises downstream tubular/Bowman pressure and opposes filtration, so it does not increase GFR.

Ureteric stone causes a reduction in glomerular filtration rate (GFR).
Following, treteral obstruction, there is a progressive fall in glomerular filtration rate (GFR) due to
a reductiorrin a single-néphron glomerular filtration rate (SNGFR) and a reduced number of
filtering nephrons.
All the other factors/options increase GFR.
emphasis: A ureteric stone raises downstream tubular/Bowman pressure and opposes filtration, so it does not increase GFR

rationales.a: Increased renal blood flow can support increased glomerular filtration.
rationales.b: Moderate efferent constriction raises glomerular pressure and can increase GFR.
rationales.d: Lower plasma oncotic pressure reduces an opposing Starling force and favors filtration.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q035.takeaway: At equal size, dextran filterability ranks polycationic highest, neutral intermediate and polyanionic lowest because the GBM is negatively charged.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH34_Q035.displayText:
At equal size, dextran filterability ranks polycationic highest, neutral intermediate and polyanionic lowest because the GBM is negatively charged.

In the given graph, the order of filterability is A>B>C, which likely indicates that the
substances are Polycationic, Neutral, Polyanionic.
The glomerular filtration barrier is negatively charged, which will repel most of the negative
charged (anionic substances). Whereas, the cationic substances are easily filtered.
Hence, the order of filterability would be: Polycationic > Neutral > Polyanionic, represented
by A, B, and C in the graph shown.
The glomerular filtration barrier consists of:

¢ Endothelium of the capillary
* Basement membrane:
¢ Lamina densa - electron-dense layer. It contains type IV collagen
¢ Lamina rara interna - contains glycosaminoglycan heparan sulfate which has a negative charge
¢ Lamina rara externa - contains glycosaminoglycan heparan sulfate which has a negative charge
¢ Layer of epithelial cells (podocytes) surrounding the outer surface of the capillary basement
membrane
The capillary endothelium is perforated by thousands of small holes called fenestrae, which
measure from 4 nm up to 8nm. Therefore, neutral substances with molecular diameters of less
than 4 nm are freely filtered, and filtration of those with diameters of more than-8nm approaches
zero. - €
However, in addition to the size of the particles, the filtration also depefds mainly on the charge
of the particle being filtered. The glomerular capillary wall consists-of-highly negatively charged
proteins called sialoproteins, which repel the negatively charged*substances (anions). The
property can be studied by using charged dextran. ae oo!
When the filtration of the negatively and positively charged dextrans Was studied, the results
indicated that the negatively chargeddextrans inthe blood are repelled, with the result that
filtration of anionic substances 4*nm in diameter is less than,half that of neutral substances of the
same size. oO a “~*
This explains, why albumin despite having an effective molecular diameter of approximately 7
nm, has a very low filtration rate. c= ° \
emphasis: At equal size, dextran filterability ranks polycationic highest, neutral intermediate and polyanionic lowest because the GBM is negatively charged

rationales.b: This reverses charge selectivity: anionic dextran is least filtered, not most.
rationales.c: Neutral dextran is intermediate; it does not filter more than polycationic material.
rationales.d: Polycationic dextran is favored by the negative barrier, so it cannot be last.
